payload.task_text:
Hi, I manage the HR analytics team and we need a department-level performance review package for the upcoming leadership meeting. Our company data warehouse has an employees table that includes each person's department, performance rating on a 1 to 5 scale, and salary information.

Please pull the employee data from the data warehouse and create an Excel workbook called Performance_Review.xlsx in the workspace. It should have two sheets.

The first sheet should be named "By Department" and contain columns Department, Total_Employees, Avg_Rating (average performance rating rounded to 2 decimal places), Top_Performers_Count (count of employees with a performance rating of 4 or 5), and Avg_Salary (average salary rounded to 2 decimal places). Sort the rows alphabetically by Department.

The second sheet should be named "Summary" and contain two columns: Metric and Value. Include the following rows: Total_Employees (total number across all departments), Overall_Avg_Rating (overall average performance rating rounded to 2 decimal places), Total_Top_Performers (total count of employees rated 4 or 5), and Overall_Avg_Salary (overall average salary rounded to 2 decimal places).

Next, create a PowerPoint presentation called Performance_Review.pptx in the workspace. Start with a title slide that says "Employee Performance Review" as the title and "Department-Level Analysis" as the subtitle. Then add one slide for each department in alphabetical order, with the department name as the slide title and the body showing that department's total employees, average rating, top performers count, and average salary. End with a summary slide titled "Overall Summary" that shows the company-wide totals for total employees, overall average rating, total top performers, and overall average salary. Make sure this summary slide states the actual computed numbers — total employees, overall average rating, total top performers, and overall average salary — as explicit numeric values consistent with the Summary sheet in the Excel workbook, not just qualitative descriptions.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, complete it directly in the main agent; do not dispatch sub-agents. Run one set-based department aggregate plus one company-wide aggregate, preserve the exact returned department labels including `R&D`, and freeze alphabetically sorted rows with all four summary metrics before writing either file. Create `Performance_Review.xlsx` and `Performance_Review.pptx` as independent native-parallel output branches from that same table. Use bulk sheet writes for the exact two Excel sheets. For the deck, use one presentation ID, add the title slide, one slide per exact department, and `Overall Summary`, and place the four explicit numeric company values on the final slide. Save once and read each artifact back once; verify exact department-name coverage and numeric consistency without a separate repair or verification phase.

Create an Excel workbook at exactly this path:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-sf-hr-performance-ppt/workspace/Performance_Review.xlsx

Use the excel MCP tools (mcp__excel__create_workbook, mcp__excel__create_worksheet, mcp__excel__write_data_to_excel, mcp__excel__rename_worksheet) to build it. If create_workbook creates a default sheet (e.g. "Sheet1"), rename it to "By Department" or delete it and create a properly named one — the final workbook must contain EXACTLY two sheets named "By Department" and "Summary".

Sheet 1 — name: "By Department"
Header row (row 1), exactly these columns:
Department | Total_Employees | Avg_Rating | Top_Performers_Count | Avg_Salary

Data rows (alphabetical by department), with numeric values as numbers (not text):
Engineering | 7096 | 3.21 | 2535 | 58991.61
Finance | 7148 | 3.21 | 2510 | 57878.19
HR | 7077 | 3.2 | 2485 | 58920.45
Operations | 7120 | 3.18 | 2426 | 57808.74
R&D | 7083 | 3.2 | 2478 | 57905.93
Sales | 7232 | 3.19 | 2523 | 58864.79
Support | 7244 | 3.2 | 2515 | 58400.48

(Note: for HR, R&D, Support write 3.2; the value represents average rating rounded to 2 decimals = 3.20. You may write 3.2 or 3.20 — both are fine numerically.)

Sheet 2 — name: "Summary"
Header row (row 1), exactly these columns:
Metric | Value

Rows (Metric as text, Value as number):
Total_Employees | 50000
Overall_Avg_Rating | 3.2
Total_Top_Performers | 17472
Overall_Avg_Salary | 58396.14

Requirements:
- Values must be written as numeric cells, not strings, so they can be computed on.
- The workbook file must exist at the specified path when done.
- Do not add any extra sheets, columns, or rows beyond what is specified.

After building, verify by reading back the workbook (e.g. mcp__excel__read_data_from_excel on both sheets or get_workbook_metadata) and confirm the two sheets exist with the correct content. Report the final file path and the verification result in your conclusion.
Build Performance_Review.xlsx

Create a PowerPoint presentation at exactly this path:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-sf-hr-performance-ppt/workspace/Performance_Review.pptx

Use the pptx MCP tools (mcp__pptx__create_presentation, mcp__pptx__add_slide, mcp__pptx__populate_placeholder / mcp__pptx__add_bullet_points / mcp__pptx__manage_text, mcp__pptx__save_presentation). The final deck must contain 9 slides in this order:

Slide 1 (title slide):
- Title: "Employee Performance Review"
- Subtitle: "Department-Level Analysis"

Slides 2–8 (one per department, in this exact alphabetical order — Engineering, Finance, HR, Operations, R&D, Sales, Support):
- Slide title = department name (e.g. "Engineering")
- Body shows that department's metrics as explicit numeric values with labels, e.g. bullet points:
  • Total Employees: 7096
  • Average Rating: 3.21
  • Top Performers Count: 2535
  • Average Salary: 58991.61

Department data (use exactly these numbers):
Engineering: 7096, 3.21, 2535, 58991.61
Finance: 7148, 3.21, 2510, 57878.19
HR: 7077, 3.2, 2485, 58920.45
Operations: 7120, 3.18, 2426, 57808.74
R&D: 7083, 3.2, 2478, 57905.93
Sales: 7232, 3.19, 2523, 58864.79
Support: 7244, 3.2, 2515, 58400.48

Slide 9 (summary slide):
- Title: "Overall Summary"
- Body must show the company-wide totals as explicit numeric values (not qualitative descriptions), e.g.:
  • Total Employees: 50000
  • Overall Average Rating: 3.2
  • Total Top Performers: 17472
  • Overall Average Salary: 58396.14

Requirements:
- Every slide must have its title and body text properly populated (use placeholders or text boxes as appropriate).
- Save the file to the exact path above with mcp__pptx__save_presentation.
- Do not add extra slides.

After saving, verify by opening/reading back the presentation (e.g. mcp__pptx__extract_presentation_text or get_presentation_info) and confirm 9 slides with the correct titles and content. Report the final file path and verification result in your conclusion.
Build Performance_Review.pptx
